author: Cyril of Alexandria
occasion: The surviving fragments comment on Daniel's vision of the Ancient of Days and the Son of Man, explaining how the Son's coming to the Ancient of Days is not spatial but refers to his entering the Father's glory.
argument: Cyril interprets the boast of the little horn in Daniel as arrogance against God's glory and against the ruler set over those from Israel, as though that ruler could not benefit his own people. He explains the opening of the books at the incarnation: the Father opened the books when the Only-Begotten came in human form, releasing sinners from judgment and enrolling the courageous among the heavenly choirs. He then raises the question of whether the Son's coming to the Ancient of Days is spatial, and rejects this as foolish because the divine is not in a place but fills all things. In the subsequent fragments, he answers that the Son came to the Father's glory, as shown by the words that to him was given honor and kingdom, and by the Father's invitation to sit at his right hand.

outline.move: Explains the boast against God's glory and the ruler of those from Israel, interprets the opening of the books at the incarnation, and raises the question of whether the Son's coming to the Ancient of Days is spatial, rejecting that as foolish.
Answers that the Son came to the Father's glory, citing the giving of honor and kingdom and the invitation to sit at God's right hand.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἕως τοῦ Παλαιοῦ τῶν ἡμερῶν ἔφθασεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The phrase 'ὁ Παλαιὸς τῶν ἡμερῶν' (the Ancient of Days) refers to the Father, but the source form should be 'Παλαιοῦ' (genitive) or the full phrase 'ὁ Παλαιὸς τῶν ἡμερῶν'; more importantly, the brief should note that Cyril explicitly rejects taking this spatially: 'ὅτι μὴ ἐν τόπῳ τὸ Θεῖον'

_unresolved_facts.claim: Scripture (Psalms): 'Quoted directly with the phrase 'Sit at my right hand.''
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου
_unresolved_facts.fix: The quotation is from Psalm 109 LXX (Psalm 110 MT/English), but it is introduced as the Father's speech: 'Ἤκουσε γὰρ τοῦ Πατρὸς λέγοντος' ('For he heard the Father saying'). The voice is better described as 'God the Father' or 'The Father speaking in Scripture,' not simply 'Scripture (Psalms).' The Psalm quotation is mediated through Cyril's framing as the Father's direct speech to the Son.

_unresolved_facts.claim: He explains the opening of the books at the incarnation: the Father opened the books when the Only-Begotten came in human form, releasing sinners from judgment and enrolling the courageous among the heavenly choirs.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἀνῆκε μὲν τοῦ κρίνεσθαι τοὺς ἐνόχους ἁμαρτίαις, ἐφῆκε δὲ τοῖς ἀνδριζομένοις τὸ ἐγγράφεσθαί τε καὶ ἐναριθμεῖσθαι λοιπὸν τοῖς ἄνω χοροῖς καὶ ἐν μνήμῃ κεῖσθαι
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source says the Father 'released those liable to judgment for sins' (ἀνῆκε μὲν τοῦ κρίνεσθαι τοὺς ἐνόχους ἁμαρτίαις) and 'permitted the courageous to be enrolled and numbered among the upper choirs and to be kept in memory.' The brief's 'releasing sinners from judgment' is slightly loose; 'those liable to judgment for sins' or 'the guilty for sins' is more precise. Also, 'enrolling the courageous among the heavenly choirs' should note ἐφῆκε ('permitted, allowed') not a direct action of enrollment.
